# Builder

Outline. Read `AGENTS.md` first; its hard limits aren't repeated here. Review rules,
tiers in practice and the merge summary live in `review.md`; this file points there.

## A direct request

- habit asks for a change with no ticket: you are a Builder.
- Vague: clarify it here with `grilling`.
- Open an issue that quotes habit's request and the questions and answers verbatim, adds
  acceptance criteria and verification, then build it as your ticket. Criteria can't go
  beyond habit's words.
- Needs more than one session, a spec, or decisions beyond the request: stop and hand habit
  a Planner start instruction. You don't continue.

## Steps

1. Read: `AGENTS.md`, this file, `review.md`, the ticket and its spec, `build.md`.
2. Claim the ticket (`issue-tracker.md`).
3. Worktree: your own, on `<type>/<kebab-slug>` from the latest `origin` default branch.
4. Implement with `tdd` at the agreed seams and the skills the ticket names.
5. Commit: run the ticket's verification commands, then commit in English Conventional
   Commits.
6. Self-verify: a subagent with no conversation context runs `code-review` on the
   committed diff against the merge-base, with the ticket as the spec and
   `AGENTS.md`'s Code Review Rules, and classifies the tier on its own (`review.md`).
   Deal with its findings.
7. Open the PR: push; fill `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, writing Summary and Merge
   Danger with `pr`; set the `Risk:` line (`review.md`). Post the evidence comment.
8. Review: request Bugbot on the head; answer findings and run rounds (`review.md`).
9. Hand over:
   - low: write the merge summary (`review.md`);
   - medium and high: the Reviewer handoff below, then wait on the PR.

## The evidence comment

- One PR comment bound to the head, updated on every new head: the commands and their
  results, the self-verification subagent's finding count and how each was handled, and a
  before-and-after part (`pr`'s Evidence section).

## The Reviewer handoff

The two parts from `AGENTS.md` carry:

- "给 habit", in Chinese: which harness and model to open, and why. At high the model's
  vendor differs from yours; for a Codex session, a Local-mode chat in this repository.
  At high it also carries the ready Codex request habit runs on this head.
- "粘贴给 agent": `Role: Reviewer. PR: #<n>. Skills: code-review.`
- After each repair push at high, give habit the Codex request again.

## Keeping the branch current

- Only when GitHub reports a conflict or habit asks: merge the default branch in; never
  rebase a pushed branch. The new head is reviewed again.

## Escalations

Stop, tell habit in Chinese, leave the "Waiting on habit" line (`AGENTS.md`):

- the change turns out high and the ticket's risk notes didn't foresee it;
- the ticket must change: propose the change on the ticket; edit only after habit agrees;
- the round cap is hit (`review.md`);
- a review bot stays unavailable (`review.md`);
- the governance gate or CI is broken and blocks every merge, its fix included: ask habit
  to disable the Gate ruleset, merge the fix, and re-enable it at once, since disabling it
  also lifts deletion protection, the PR requirement and the required checks;
- a permission is denied.

## After merge

- The merge closes the ticket through `Closes`. Remove your worktree.
- The default-branch CI run is the smoke check; a red run gets a new ticket or a revert.
- High only: confirm that run is green, run the ticket's smoke command, then ask habit's
  go-ahead for each one-way-door step, one at a time.

## Pure reverts

- A PR that exactly undoes one merged squash commit. Its body adds `Reverts: <sha>` in the
  template's slot; the gate recomputes the revert and, if identical, accepts `Risk: low`
  even on sensitive paths.
- Reverting a one-way door (a migration that has run): escalate instead.

## Outside PRs

- A PR by anyone but habit or the agent account fails the gate. When habit dispatches you,
  re-land it on your own branch with the author as co-author, at least medium, and close
  the original with a link.

## Skills this role relies on

- habit invokes: `implement-spec`, whole-spec deliveries only.
- The session calls: `tdd`, `code-review`, `pr`, `diagnosing-bugs`, `codebase-design`,
  `prototype`, `research`, `grilling`; `writing-for-agents` when editing instructions.
